words.ex: I have math lesson every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 我每周一都有数学课。
words.en: A lesson is a period of time in which someone is taught about a particular subject or how to do something.

words.tr:
n. 组；群；集团；
v. （使）形成组；
words.ex: The students are in a group of five.
words.ex_cn: 这些学生组成一个五人小组。
words.en: A group is a number of people or things that are located, gathered, or classed together.

words.ex: He sat with good posture at the desk.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在书桌前，姿势端正。
words.en: Your posture is the way in which you hold your body when you are standing or sitting.

words.ex: He conveyed his thanks with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着表达了谢意。
words.en: If you convey information or a message, you communicate it to someone, often in a way that is not direct.

words.ex: This book belongs to the science category.
words.ex_cn: 这本书属于科学类别。
words.en: A category is a class or group of things that have similar characteristics.

words.ex: The government kept the mission in secrecy.
words.ex_cn: 政府将这次任务保密。
words.en: Secrecy is the practice of keeping something secret, or the state of being secret.

words.ex: He has a nasal voice when he has a cold.
words.ex_cn: 他感冒时声音有鼻音。
words.en: Nasal is used to describe something relating to the nose or the production of sound through the nose.

words.ex: They share intimacy through quiet talks at night.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过夜晚的安静交谈建立亲密感。
words.en: A close, familiar, and usually affectionate or loving personal relationship with another person or group.

words.ex: He made a gesture of welcome with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他用手做了一个欢迎的姿态。
words.en: A gesture is a movement that you make with a part of your body, especially your hands, to express emotion or information.

words.tr:
n. 耸肩
v. 耸肩
words.ex: He shrugged when asked why he was late.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到为什么迟到时，他耸了耸肩。
words.en: If you shrug, you raise your shoulders to show that you are not interested in something or that you do not know or care about something.

words.tr:
n. 抓痕；刮伤；
v. 抓搔；刮；
words.ex: The cat left a scratch on the door.
words.ex_cn: 猫在门上抓出了一道抓痕。
words.en: If you scratch something, you rub your fingernails or claws against it, often because it is itchy or irritating.

words.ex: The proximity of the school to the park makes it nice for kids.
words.ex_cn: 学校靠近公园，对孩子们来说很好。
words.en: Proximity refers to the state of being near in space or time.

words.ex: The cat hunched its back when it saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 猫看到狗时，背部拱了起来。
words.en: A hunch is a feeling or guess based on intuition rather than known facts.

words.ex: The dark clouds indicate rain.
words.ex_cn: 乌云表明要下雨了。
words.en: If one thing indicates another, the first thing shows that the second is true or exists.

words.ex: The necklace is an imitation made of plastic.
words.ex_cn: 这条项链是用塑料做的仿制品。
words.en: An imitation of something is a copy of it.

words.tr: n. 嘲笑；愚弄；被嘲笑的对象
words.ex: He laughed in mockery of her mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他嘲笑她的错误。
words.en: Mockery is the act of mocking someone or something or the state of being mocked.

words.tr:
v. 补充；与…相辅相成；
n. 补足物；补语；余角；
words.ex: The red scarf complements her blue coat.
words.ex_cn: 这条红围巾补充了她的蓝外套。
words.en: To complement something means to make it complete or perfect by adding something to it.

words.ex: The two companies will merge next year.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司明年将合并。
words.en: To combine or unite to form a single entity.

words.ex: The mixture is homogeneous and looks the same throughout.
words.ex_cn: 这种混合物是均一的，看起来处处都一样。
words.en: Something that is homogeneous is uniform in nature or character throughout.

words.tr: adj. 不同的；多种多样的；
words.ex: The class has diverse students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级有来自许多国家的不同学生。
words.en: If a group or range of things is diverse, it is made up of a wide variety of things.

words.tr:
v. 见证；
n. 证人；目击者；
words.ex: He witnessed the accident yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天目睹了那起事故。
words.en: A witness is someone who sees an event happen, especially a crime or an accident. Witnesses are often called upon to give evidence in court.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；彻底的；激进的；
words.ex: The government made radical changes to the education system.
words.ex_cn: 政府对教育系统进行了根本性的改革。
words.en: A radical change or difference is very big and important.

words.ex: He faced racial discrimination at work.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中遭遇了种族歧视。
words.en: Relating to the common characteristics of different races of people, especially in the context of social or cultural differences.

words.ex: It is evident that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is evident, it is easy to see, perceive, or understand.

words.ex: The immigrant found a job in the city.
words.ex_cn: 这位移民在城市里找到了一份工作。
words.en: An immigrant is a person who comes to live permanently in a foreign country.

words.tr: adj. 完全的；荒凉的；光秃秃的；僵硬的；严厉的
words.ex: There was a stark difference between the two results.
words.ex_cn: 这两个结果之间有完全的差异。
words.en: Stark means complete, severe, or obvious in a way that is impossible to avoid noticing.

words.ex: He follows a systematic approach to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种系统的方法来解决数学问题。
words.en: A systematic approach or method is one that is done according to a fixed plan, in a thorough and efficient way.

words.ex: The company values innovation in its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司重视产品的创新。
words.en: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things.

words.ex: He bought a new device to take photos.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一个新设备来拍照。
words.en: A device is an object or machine that has been invented for a particular purpose.

words.tr: adj. 精密复杂的；老练的；
words.ex: The phone has a sophisticated camera.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个精密复杂的摄像头。
words.en: A sophisticated person is intelligent and knows a lot, so that they are able to understand complicated situations. A sophisticated machine, device, or method is more advanced or complex than others.

words.ex: He embeds the photo in the document.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片插入到文档中。
words.en: To fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass.

words.ex: The price of bread went up because of inflation.
words.ex_cn: 由于通货膨胀，面包的价格上涨了。
words.en: Inflation is a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.

words.ex: He made an investment in a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他投资了一家小企业。
words.en: An investment is an amount of money that you invest in something.

words.ex: The volcano erupts suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 火山突然喷发。
words.en: If a volcano erupts, it throws out smoke, fire, and melted rocks.

words.ex: The police told everyone to evacuate the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察让所有人撤离大楼。
words.en: To evacuate means to remove people from a place of danger to a safer place.

words.ex: The navy launched a large fleet to protect the coast.
words.ex_cn: 海军派出了一支大型舰队来保护海岸。
words.en: A fleet is a group of ships or vehicles that are controlled by one company or organization and are used for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He rides a rickshaw to the market.
words.ex_cn: 他坐人力车去市场。
words.en: A rickshaw is a small, light vehicle with two wheels that is pulled by one person and used for carrying passengers, especially in Asian countries.

words.tr:
v. 拖；拉；拖运；
n. 拖；拉；拖运；
words.ex: He hauled the heavy box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他把沉重的箱子拖过了房间。
words.en: To haul something means to pull it or carry it with a lot of effort.

words.tr:
n. V字形刻痕；等级；切口
v. 赢得；刻凹痕
words.ex: He made a notch on the stick to count days.
words.ex_cn: 他在木棍上刻了一个刻痕来计数天数。
words.en: A notch is a small cut or indentation in a surface. It can also refer to a level or degree in a scale or a narrow pass between mountains.

words.tr:
n. 接触（的机会或权利）；进入；通道；
v. 获取；使用；接近；
words.ex: Students need access to the library.
words.ex_cn: 学生需要有接触图书馆的机会。
words.en: If you have access to a building or other place, you are able to enter it or use it.

words.tr:
n. 摊位；
v. 故意拖延；
words.ex: He sells fruits at a stall in the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场的一个摊位上卖水果。
words.en: A stall is a small open-fronted shop or a compartment for one animal in a stable or barn. As a verb, it means to stop or cause to stop making progress.

words.tr:
n. 购买；采购；
v. 购买；采购；
words.ex: The purchase of a new car took all his savings.
words.ex_cn: 买一辆新车花光了他所有的积蓄。
words.en: To purchase something means to buy it. It can also refer to something that has been bought.

words.tr: n. 所有者；经营者 ；业主
words.ex: The proprietor runs a small coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 店主经营一家小咖啡馆。
words.en: A proprietor is a person who owns a particular type of business, especially a hotel, a shop, or a company.

words.tr: n. 保持器；保留金；家仆
words.ex: The dentist gave me a retainer to wear at night.
words.ex_cn: 牙医给了我一个保持器，让我晚上戴着。
words.en: A retainer is a fee that you pay to someone in order to make sure that they will be available to do work for you when you need them to.

words.ex: The rain caused a torrent down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨在山间形成了一股急流。
words.en: A torrent is a fast-moving stream of water or other liquid.

words.ex: The country enjoys prosperity after years of peace.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在多年的和平后迎来了繁荣。
words.en: Prosperity is a condition in which a person, community, or country is thriving and successful, especially in financial terms.

words.ex: The city needs better infrastructure for roads and water.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市需要更好的道路和供水设施。
words.en: The basic physical and organizational structures and facilities (e.g., buildings, roads, power supplies) needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.

words.ex: Going first is a privilege, not a right.
words.ex_cn: 优先权是一种特权，而不是权利。
words.en: A privilege is a special right or advantage that only one person or group has.

words.ex: The school prohibits students from using phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If a law or someone in authority prohibits something, they forbid it or make it illegal.

words.ex: He offended the law by stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他偷窃触犯了法律。
words.en: If you offend someone, you upset or embarrass them by saying or doing something that they think is rude or insulting.

words.ex: He tries not to demean his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他尽量不贬低他的同学。
words.en: To demean someone or something means to cause them to lose their dignity or respect.

words.ex: This is a genuine diamond.
words.ex_cn: 这是一颗真正的钻石。
words.en: If something is genuine, it is real and exactly what it appears to be.

words.ex: The child gave a naive smile when he believed the story.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子相信这个故事时，他露出了天真的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as naïve, you think they lack experience and so expect things to be easy or people to be honest or kind.

words.tr:
adj. 认命的；顺从的；勉强接受的
v. 辞职；“resign”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was resigned to losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他认命地接受了输掉比赛的结果。
words.en: If you are resigned to an unpleasant situation or fact, you accept it without complaining because you realize that you cannot change it.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；临近的；
words.ex: An imminent storm is coming soon.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴很快就要来了。
words.en: If you say that something is imminent, especially something unpleasant, you mean it is almost certain to happen very soon.

words.ex: The migrant found a new job in the city.
words.ex_cn: 这位移居者在城市里找到了一份新工作。
words.en: A migrant is a person who moves from one place to another, especially in order to find work.

words.tr:
n. 厚木底皮鞋；木屐
v. 堵塞；妨碍
words.ex: She wore wooden clogs to work in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着厚木底皮鞋去花园干活。
words.en: If something clogs a hole or place, it blocks it so that nothing can pass through.

words.ex: He opened his umbrella when it started to rain.
words.ex_cn: 天下雨时，他打开了伞。
words.en: An umbrella is a device consisting of a circular canopy of fabric on a folding metal frame, used as protection against rain or sunlight.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.ex: He is a consultant for a big company.
words.ex_cn: 他是这家大公司的顾问。
words.en: A consultant is a person who gives expert advice to a person or organization on a particular subject.

words.ex: Smartphones supplanted landline phones.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机取代了固定电话。
words.en: To supplant someone or something means to take the place of them, often by being more powerful or effective.

words.tr:
n. 法令；判决
v. 判决；颁布；裁定
words.ex: The king issued a decree to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 国王发布了一项法令来停止战争。
words.en: An official order issued by a legal authority.

words.ex: The municipal library is open every day.
words.ex_cn: 这座市政图书馆每天都开放。
words.en: Relating to a city or town or its governing body.

words.tr: v. 恢复；修复；改造（罪犯）
words.ex: The hospital will rehabilitate the injured athlete.
words.ex_cn: 医院将帮助受伤的运动员康复。
words.en: To rehabilitate someone who has been ill or in prison means to help them to live a normal life again. To rehabilitate a building or an area means to improve its condition.

words.tr: v. 追溯到；“date”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 过时的；陈旧的；
words.ex: This coin is dated to the year 1500.
words.ex_cn: 这枚硬币追溯到1500年。
words.en: Something that is dated is old-fashioned and no longer relevant or useful.

words.ex: He wore a decent shirt to the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件像样的衬衫去面试。
words.en: Decent is used to describe something which is considered to be of an acceptable standard or quality.

words.tr: n. 住处；膳宿；(交通工具内的)空间；
words.ex: The hotel provided cheap accommodation for travelers.
words.ex_cn: 酒店为旅客提供了便宜的住处。
words.en: Accommodation is a place where someone lives or stays, or the act of providing someone with a place to live or stay.

words.ex: His loyalty to his friends never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的忠诚从未改变。
words.en: The quality of being loyal to someone or something.

words.ex: He votes in a democratic election.
words.ex_cn: 他在民主选举中投票。
words.en: A democratic country, government, or political system is governed by representatives who are elected by the people.

words.ex: This brand has an exclusive design.
words.ex_cn: 这个品牌拥有独有的设计。
words.en: Something that is exclusive is available only to particular people, and not to everyone.

words.ex: The boy resembles his father.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩长得像他父亲。
words.en: If one thing or person resembles another, they are similar to each other.

words.ex: The elite of the city often meet at private clubs.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的精英经常在私人俱乐部会面。
words.en: You can refer to the most powerful, rich, or talented people within a particular group, place, or society as the elite.

words.ex: He decided to embark on a new career.
words.ex_cn: 他决定从事一份新职业。
words.en: To embark on something means to start it, especially something new, difficult, or exciting.

words.tr:
n. 教练；长途客运汽车；
v. 训练；培训；
words.ex: The coach taught the team how to win.
words.ex_cn: 教练教球队如何获胜。
words.en: A coach is someone who trains a person or team in a particular sport. It also refers to a large, comfortable bus that carries passengers on long journeys.

words.tr:
n. 服务人员
adj. 随之而来的
words.ex: The attendant helped me find my seat.
words.ex_cn: 服务员帮我找到了座位。
words.en: An attendant is someone whose job is to serve or help people in a public place.

words.ex: It is illegal to drive without a license.
words.ex_cn: 无证驾驶是非法的。
words.en: If something is illegal, the law says that it is not allowed.

words.tr:
adj. 肮脏恶臭的；
v. 对…犯规；
words.ex: The foul smell came from the garbage bin.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自垃圾桶。
words.en: If you describe something as foul, you mean it is dirty and smells or tastes unpleasant. In sports, a foul is an act that is against the rules of the game.

words.tr:
n. 成分；
adj. 构成的；
words.ex: Sugar is a constituent of soda.
words.ex_cn: 糖是苏打水的一种成分。
words.en: A constituent is a part of a whole. In politics, a constituent is a person who is represented by an elected official.

words.ex: The hapless boy lost his wallet and got caught in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 这个倒霉的男孩丢了钱包，还被雨淋了。
words.en: If you describe someone as hapless, you mean that they are unlucky or unfortunate.

words.tr:
n. 妥协；
v. 危及；
words.ex: They reached a compromise after hours of talk.
words.ex_cn: 经过数小时的讨论，他们达成了妥协。
words.en: A compromise is an agreement between two people or groups in which each side gives up some of the things they want so that both sides are happy at the end.

words.ex: A gentle breeze blew through the trees.
words.ex_cn: 一阵微风轻轻吹过树梢。
words.en: A breeze is a gentle wind.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.tr:
adj. 困惑的；发呆的
v. 使困惑；使茫然；“bemuse”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He looked bemused when the teacher asked a strange question.
words.ex_cn: 当老师问了一个奇怪的问题时，他看起来很困惑。
words.en: If you are bemused, you are puzzled or confused.

words.ex: The local company is an affiliate of the big global brand.
words.ex_cn: 这家本地公司是这个全球大品牌的分公司。
words.en: If an organization is affiliated with another larger organization, it is officially connected with the larger organization or is a member of it.

words.tr:
v. 轻声笑；咯咯笑；暗自笑
n. 暗自发笑；咯咯声
words.ex: He chuckled when he saw the funny dog.
words.ex_cn: 他看到那只搞笑的狗时笑了起来。
words.en: To laugh quietly or inwardly.

words.tr:
v. （使）获得；
adj. 安全的；稳定的；
words.ex: He worked hard to secure a job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以获得一份工作。
words.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

words.ex: He is a prospective student at Harvard.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的预期学生。
words.en: Prospective is used to describe someone or something that is expected or likely to happen or be in the future.

words.ex: He is a scientist of great renown.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位享有盛誉的科学家。
words.en: Renown is the state of being known and talked about by many people because of your achievements, qualities, or actions.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.ex: He is literally the best player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他确实是队里最好的球员。
words.en: In a literal manner or sense; exactly.

words.ex: The axe will cleave the wood in two.
words.ex_cn: 斧头会把木头劈成两半。
words.en: To split or sever something, especially along a natural line or grain; to adhere firmly and closely or loyally and unwaveringly to something.

words.ex: The company follows ethical practices in hiring.
words.ex_cn: 该公司在招聘中遵循伦理规范。
words.en: Relating to moral principles or the branch of knowledge dealing with these.

words.tr: v. 委托；交付；托运；寄售
words.ex: He will consign the package to the post office.
words.ex_cn: 他将把包裹寄到邮局。
words.en: If you consign something to someone, you give it to them to keep or to sell.

words.tr: v. 制定法律；用立法规定
words.ex: The government will legislate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将制定新规则。
words.en: To legislate means to make or enact laws.

words.tr:
n. 违背；
v. 攻破；
words.ex: The company committed a breach of contract.
words.ex_cn: 该公司违反了合同。
words.en: A breach of a law, rule, or agreement is an act of breaking it.

words.ex: The government gave amnesty to political prisoners.
words.ex_cn: 政府向政治犯提供了赦免。
words.en: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to a group of people by a government, especially for political offenses.

words.tr: phrase. 第2课第1组；第二课第一组
words.ex: Lesson 2 Group 1 finished their math homework.
words.ex_cn: 第2课第1组完成了他们的数学作业。
words.en: A designated set of students or participants in the second lesson of a course or training program.

words.ex: The dictionary gives a clear definition of the word.
words.ex_cn: 词典给出了这个词的清晰定义。
words.en: A statement of the exact meaning of a word, phrase, or concept.

words.ex: He did a preliminary test before the main experiment.
words.ex_cn: 他在主要实验之前做了一个初步测试。
words.en: Preliminary means something that is done or happens before the main part or event, especially as an introduction or preparation.

words.ex: The study uses a new methodology to collect data.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究使用了一种新的方法论来收集数据。
words.en: A methodology is a system of methods and principles for doing something, for example for teaching or for carrying out research.

words.ex: He made a hypothesis that plants grow faster in light.
words.ex_cn: 他提出一个假设，认为植物在光照下长得更快。
words.en: A hypothesis is an idea which is suggested as a possible explanation for a particular situation or condition, but which has not yet been proved to be correct.

words.ex: The mountain has great prominence in the landscape.
words.ex_cn: 这座山在景观中十分突出。
words.en: If someone or something is in a position of prominence, they are important or well-known.

words.ex: The boy found a fossil in the rock.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在岩石中发现了一块化石。
words.en: A fossil is the remains or impression of a prehistoric organism preserved in petrified form or as a mold or cast in rock.

words.ex: Carbon dioxide makes the air warm.
words.ex_cn: 二氧化碳使空气变暖。
words.en: A compound containing two atoms of oxygen combined with another element or group.

words.tr:
n. 蓄意破坏
v. 蓄意破坏；暗中破坏
words.ex: He tried to sabotage the project.
words.ex_cn: 他试图破坏这个项目。
words.en: Sabotage is the act of deliberately destroying, damaging, or obstructing something, especially for political or military advantage.

words.ex: The train will derail if the tracks are broken.
words.ex_cn: 如果铁轨损坏，火车就会脱轨。
words.en: To cause a train or other vehicle to leave its tracks accidentally; to divert or cause to deviate from an intended course.

words.tr: adj. 不安全的；危险的；不稳当的；
words.ex: The ladder was precarious and might fall.
words.ex_cn: 梯子不安全，可能会倒。
words.en: If a situation is precarious, it is uncertain or dangerous, and could get worse or fail.

words.tr: adj. 外来的；外国来的；奇异的；
words.ex: The market sells exotic fruits from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个市场出售来自其他国家的外来水果。
words.en: Something that is exotic is unusual and interesting because it comes from or is related to a distant country.

words.tr:
n. 修指甲
v. 修指甲；修剪
words.ex: She got a manicure on Saturday.
words.ex_cn: 她在周六做了美甲。
words.en: A manicure is a cosmetic beauty treatment for the fingernails and hands performed at home or in a nail salon.

words.ex: He walked down the wide boulevard with many shops.
words.ex_cn: 他沿着满是商店的宽阔大马路散步。
words.en: A boulevard is a wide street in a city, usually with trees along the sides.

words.tr: n. 历史遗迹；纪念碑；不朽作品；
words.ex: The ancient monument attracts many tourists each year.
words.ex_cn: 这座古代历史遗迹每年吸引许多游客。
words.en: A monument is a large structure, usually made of stone, which is built to remind people of an important person or event.

words.tr: n. 特性；怪癖；奇异之物
words.ex: One peculiarity of the old house is its red door.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子的一个特点是它的红门。
words.en: A peculiarity is a characteristic or quality that is distinctive or unique to a particular person, place, or thing.

words.tr: adj. 谨慎的；慎重的；精明的
words.ex: He is prudent with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他在花钱时很谨慎。
words.en: If you are prudent, you are careful and avoid taking unnecessary risks.

words.tr: v. 接种疫苗；预防接种
words.ex: The doctor will vaccinate the child tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 医生明天会给这个孩子接种疫苗。
words.en: To vaccinate someone is to give them a vaccine, usually by injection, to prevent them from getting a disease.

words.ex: Wear a helmet as a precaution when riding a bike.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔作为一种预防措施。
words.en: A precaution is an action that is intended to prevent something dangerous or unpleasant from happening.

words.ex: He ate excessive amounts of candy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了过多的糖果。
words.en: If you describe the amount or level of something as excessive, you disapprove of it because it is more or higher than is necessary or reasonable.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
n. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
words.ex: They stroll in the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他们晚饭后在公园里闲逛。
words.en: If you stroll somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.ex: The store offers an assortment of snacks.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店提供各种各样的零食。
words.en: An assortment is a group of similar things that are of different types or sizes.

words.tr: v. 强烈吸引住；使着迷；
words.ex: The magic show fascinated the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演深深吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If something fascinates you, it interests and delights you so much that your thoughts tend to concentrate on it.

words.tr: n. 迷宫；难解的事件；错综复杂；
words.ex: The child got lost in the labyrinth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A labyrinth is a complicated irregular network of passages or paths in which it is difficult to find one's way; a maze.

words.tr: phrase. 第二课第二组；第2课第2组
words.ex: The students in lesson 2 group 2 are doing their homework.
words.ex_cn: 第二课第二组的学生正在做作业。
words.en: A second designated set of students or participants in the second lesson of a course or training program.

words.ex: We bought spices at the local bazaar.
words.ex_cn: 我们在当地的集市上买了香料。
words.en: A bazaar is a market consisting of rows of shops or stalls, especially in the Middle East, or a sale of miscellaneous contributed articles to benefit some charity.

words.tr: adj. 刺鼻的；一语道破的
words.ex: The cheese has a pungent smell.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪有刺鼻的气味。
words.en: Having a sharply strong taste or smell.

words.ex: She bought a dress from a small boutique downtown.
words.ex_cn: 她在市中心的一家小型时装精品屋买了一条裙子。
words.en: A boutique is a small shop that sells stylish clothes, shoes, or jewelry.

words.ex: He goes to the mosque every Friday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周五去清真寺。
words.en: A mosque is a building where Muslims go to worship.

words.ex: The elephant is enormous.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象非常巨大。
words.en: If you describe something as enormous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size or amount.

words.ex: I caught a glimpse of the cat before it ran away.
words.ex_cn: 我在它跑掉之前瞥了一眼那只猫。
words.en: A glimpse is a brief, quick look at something or someone.

words.tr:
v. 激怒；使生气；激起
n. 怨恨；愤恨
words.ex: His rude comment piqued her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的评论激怒了她。
words.en: If something piques your interest or curiosity, it makes you interested or curious.

words.ex: She wore a warm scarf in winter.
words.ex_cn: 她在冬天戴了一条暖和的围巾。
words.en: A scarf is a piece of cloth that you wear around your neck or head, usually to keep yourself warm.

words.tr: adj. 无穷尽的；经久不衰的；永远可靠的
words.ex: Her unfailing smile made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 她永不消失的微笑让每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: If you describe someone's good qualities or behaviour as unfailing, you mean that they never change.

words.ex: He screamed in agony after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒后痛苦地大叫。
words.en: Agony is very severe physical or mental pain.

words.ex: He felt awkward when he forgot his friend's name.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记朋友的名字时，他感到很尴尬。
words.en: If you describe a situation as awkward, you mean that it is embarrassing or difficult to deal with.

words.ex: He told an anecdote about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他童年的趣事。
words.en: An anecdote is a short, amusing or interesting story about a real incident or person.

words.ex: The imperial palace was built long ago.
words.ex_cn: 这座帝国宫殿是很久以前建造的。
words.en: relating to an empire or an emperor; majestic or superior in quality or size

words.ex: The bulk of the students passed the exam.
words.ex_cn: 大部分学生通过了考试。
words.en: The bulk of something is most of it. The bulk of something is its size, especially when it is very large.

words.tr:
n. 织布机；
v. 迫近；
words.ex: The old loom made a loud clicking sound.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧织布机发出很大的咔嗒声。
words.en: If something looms over you, it appears as a large or unclear shape, often in a way that is frightening or causes worry.

words.ex: The class is learning demography from a book.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级正在从一本书中学习人口统计学。
words.en: Demography is the study of human populations, including their size, growth, density, distribution, and vital statistics.

words.ex: The hiker stood at the edge of the cliff.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者站在悬崖边上。
words.en: A cliff is a high area of rock with a very steep side, often at the edge of the sea or a river.

words.tr:
v. 派遣；调遣；发送
n. 快信；发送；派遣
words.ex: He will dispatch the package tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会寄出这个包裹。
words.en: To send someone or something to a particular place for a particular purpose.

words.ex: We have sufficient food for the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们有足够的食物用于这次旅行。
words.en: If something is sufficient for a particular purpose, there is enough of it for the purpose.

words.ex: The void on the page made the text look empty.
words.ex_cn: 页面上的空白让文字看起来空荡荡的。
words.en: If you describe a situation or a feeling as a void, you mean that it seems empty because there is nothing interesting or worthwhile about it.

words.ex: He works in the aerospace industry.
words.ex_cn: 他在航空航天行业工作。
words.en: The branch of technology and industry concerned with both aviation and space flight.

words.tr: adj. 有资格的；合格的；合意的；
words.ex: He is eligible to vote because he is 18 years old.
words.ex_cn: 他年满18岁，有资格投票。
words.en: Someone who is eligible for something is qualified or allowed to do it.

words.tr: adj. 陡峭的；急剧升降的；
words.ex: The mountain has a steep path.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一条陡峭的小路。
words.en: A steep slope or hill is one that is at a sharp angle, rather than being flat or gradual.

words.ex: He squeezed into the small seat.
words.ex_cn: 他挤进了小座位里。
words.en: To squeeze something means to press it firmly, usually with your fingers or hands, often to get liquid out of it or to make it smaller.

words.tr: phrase. 第二课第三组；课程2第3组
words.ex: Lesson 2 Group 3 is working on math problems.
words.ex_cn: 第二课第三组正在做数学题。
words.en: A third designated set of students or participants in the second lesson of a course or training program.

words.ex: This small enterprise makes handmade toys.
words.ex_cn: 这家小企业生产手工玩具。
words.en: An enterprise is a company or business, often a large one, or a difficult or important project, especially one that involves a lot of planning and organization.

words.ex: He wants to emigrate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他想移民到加拿大过更好的生活。
words.en: To leave one's own country in order to settle permanently in another.

words.ex: He is invariably late for meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他总是开会迟到。
words.en: If something invariably happens or is invariably true, it always happens or is always true.

words.ex: He is an alumnus of Harvard University.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的男毕业生。
words.en: An alumnus is a former student of a particular school, college, or university.

words.ex: The company plans to recruit new staff next month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司计划下个月招聘新员工。
words.en: To recruit means to enlist someone in the armed forces or to persuade someone to join a company, organization, or group.

words.tr:
v. 注册；登记；
n. 登记簿；
words.ex: He will register for the course next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周会注册这门课程。
words.en: If you register something, you officially record it or list it.

words.tr:
n. 跳跃；
v. 跳跃；
words.ex: The cat made a big leap over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 猫跳过了篱笆。
words.en: To leap means to jump high or a long way, or to move quickly and with a lot of energy.

words.tr: adj. 一定会；密切相关的；有义务的； v. “bind”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is bound to win the race.
words.ex_cn: 他一定会赢得比赛。
words.en: If one person, thing, or situation is bound to another, they are closely connected with each other, and it is difficult for them to be separated or to escape from each other. If you say that something is bound to happen, you mean that you are sure it will happen, because it is a natural consequence of something that is already known or exists.

words.tr:
v. 嘎吱嘎吱地动；发嘎吱嘎吱声
n. 嘎吱声；艰难局面；危急情况
words.ex: The dog crunches the bone loudly.
words.ex_cn: 狗嘎吱嘎吱地咬着骨头。
words.en: To crunch means to chew noisily with your mouth open, or to make a loud noise like the sound of something being crushed. It can also refer to a critical point or situation, especially in financial contexts.

words.ex: He will participate in the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他将参与学校的戏剧演出。
words.en: To take part in an activity or event.

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

words.tr: adj. 亲切的；和蔼的；温暖的
words.ex: He is a genial man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Friendly and cheerful.

words.ex: They conspire to cheat on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋在考试中作弊。
words.en: If two or more people or groups conspire to do something illegal or harmful, they make a secret agreement to do it.

words.ex: He refused the money purely because it was wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他纯粹是因为觉得不对才拒绝了那笔钱。
words.en: In a pure manner; without admixture or adulteration.

words.ex: He lived in a crude hut with no electricity.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个没有电的简陋小屋里。
words.en: A crude substance or product is in its natural state and has not been processed or refined.

words.ex: This phone is superior to the old one.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机比旧的更好。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as superior, you mean that they are better than other people or things.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.ex: The teacher will allocate books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将给学生分配书籍。
words.en: To allocate something means to give it to a particular person or use it for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The heat was inescapable in the small room.
words.ex_cn: 小房间里热得无法逃避。
words.en: If you describe a fact, situation, or activity as inescapable, you mean that it is difficult not to notice it or be affected by it.

words.tr: n. 倡议；主动权；自发性；措施；
words.ex: The school launched an initiative to reduce plastic use.
words.ex_cn: 学校发起了一项减少塑料使用的倡议。
words.en: An initiative is an important act or statement that is intended to solve a problem.

words.tr: adj. 不加选择的；不加区别的；
words.ex: The bombing was indiscriminate and hurt many civilians.
words.ex_cn: 这次轰炸是不加选择的，伤害了许多平民。
words.en: If you describe an action as indiscriminate, you are critical of it because it does not involve any careful thought or choice.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.tr: adj. 暂定的；不确定的；试验性的；
words.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next week.
words.ex_cn: 我们制定了一个下周见面的暂定计划。
words.en: If you make a tentative suggestion or plan, you make it without being sure that it is right or acceptable.

words.tr: adj. 色情的； 多情的； 爱情的
words.ex: The movie showed amorous scenes that shocked the audience.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了让观众震惊的色情场景。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings or actions as amorous, you mean that they involve sexual desire.

words.tr: phrase. 第2课第4组；第2课第4小组
words.ex: Lesson 2 Group 4 is working on the math project.
words.ex_cn: 第2课第4组正在做数学项目。
words.en: A fourth designated set of students or participants in the second lesson of a course or training program.

words.ex: This is an evolutionary change in the species.
words.ex_cn: 这是该物种的一种进化的改变。
words.en: Relating to or denoting processes of development or growth, especially in a biological context.

words.ex: This product is inferior to the other one.
words.ex_cn: 这个产品比另一个差。
words.en: If one person or thing is inferior to another, they are not as good, important, or valuable as the other person or thing.

words.ex: The abrasive surface wore down the metal.
words.ex_cn: 磨损的表面磨耗了金属。
words.en: An abrasive substance is rough and can be used to clean surfaces or to make them smooth by rubbing. An abrasive person is someone who is harsh and rude.

words.ex: The company will compensate you for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 公司会因延误而补偿你。
words.en: If you compensate for a lack of something or for something you have done wrong, you do something to show that you are sorry or that you are trying to make things better.

words.tr: adj. 性欲的；性爱的；色情的
words.ex: The movie contains erotic scenes that are not suitable for children.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影包含不适合儿童的色情场景。
words.en: Relating to or tending to arouse sexual desire or excitement.

words.ex: He is the recipient of the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个奖项的接受者。
words.en: A recipient is a person who receives something.

words.tr:
v. 缓慢或吃力地走
n. 长途跋涉
words.ex: He trudges through the snow every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跋涉穿过雪地。
words.en: To walk slowly and with heavy steps, typically because of exhaustion or harsh conditions.

words.ex: The lush grass looked green after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，葱翠的草地显得格外绿。
words.en: A lush area has a lot of green, healthy plants, grass, and trees.

words.tr: v. 使气馁；使胆怯；吓倒
words.ex: The loud noise did not daunt her.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音并没有吓倒她。
words.en: If something daunts you, it makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.ex: The small house is on a foothill near the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这栋小房子位于山脚下的山坡上。
words.en: A foothill is a low hill at the base of a mountain or mountain range.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.tr:
adj. 极小的；特小的；微小的
n. 小的人；指小词缀；爱称
words.ex: The diminutive cat sat on the small mat.
words.ex_cn: 那只小巧的猫坐在小垫子上。
words.en: A diminutive person or object is very small.

words.tr: n. 影响；方位；轴承；举止； v. 忍受；“bear”的现在分词；
words.ex: The new policy has a big bearing on our daily lives.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策对我们日常生活有很大影响。
words.en: The manner in which one conducts or carries oneself, including posture and gestures; also refers to a machine part that supports another part and reduces friction.

words.tr: adj. 高的；崇高的；傲慢的
words.ex: The mountain has a lofty peak.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一个很高的山顶。
words.en: If you say that someone behaves in a lofty way, you are critical of them for behaving in a proud and rather unpleasant way, as if they think they are very important.

words.tr:
n. 捆；束；包
v. 匆匆送走
words.ex: He bought a bundle of newspapers.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一捆报纸。
words.en: A bundle is a number of things that are tied or wrapped together so that they can be carried or stored easily.

words.ex: He tied the box with a red cord.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根红绳把盒子绑了起来。
words.en: A cord is a thick string or thin rope made of twisted strands, or something resembling such a string or rope in appearance or function.

words.ex: They ascribe his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他们把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you ascribe an event or condition to a particular cause, you say or consider that it was caused by that thing.

words.tr:
n. 释放；发布；
v. 释放；发布；
words.ex: The release of the prisoner made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯的释放让每个人都高兴。
words.en: To release something means to let it go or to allow it to be free, or to make something available to the public.

words.tr:
v. 挤作一团
n. 挤作一团
words.ex: The team huddled together to plan their next move.
words.ex_cn: 团队聚在一起规划下一步行动。
words.en: If people huddle together, they stand, sit, or lie close to each other because they are cold or frightened.

words.tr:
n. 鞭策；
v. 刺激；
words.ex: The competition served as a spur to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 竞争成了推动他更努力工作的鞭策。
words.en: A spur is something that makes you want to do something or that encourages you to do it. It can also refer to a sharp device worn on the heel of a rider's boot to urge a horse forward.

words.tr: adj. 宏伟的；壮丽的；威严的；
words.ex: The majestic mountain stood above the clouds.
words.ex_cn: 那座宏伟的山峰耸立在云层之上。
words.en: If you describe something as majestic, you mean that it has a quality of greatness and impressiveness that often inspires admiration or awe.

words.ex: The monks live in a quiet monastery.
words.ex_cn: 僧侣们住在一座安静的修道院里。
words.en: A monastery is a building or collection of buildings in which monks live and work.

words.ex: He surpassed his brother in math scores.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学成绩上超过了他弟弟。
words.en: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

words.tr: phrase. 第三课第一组；第3课第1组
words.ex: Lesson 3 Group 1 will present their project tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 第三课第一组明天将展示他们的项目。
words.en: A designated set of students or participants in the third lesson of a course or training program.

words.ex: His status in the company is very high.
words.ex_cn: 他在公司里的地位很高。
words.en: The status of someone or something is their position or situation according to the law or according to other people's opinions.

words.ex: The economic situation is getting worse.
words.ex_cn: 经济状况正在恶化。
words.en: Economic means concerned with the organization of the money, industry, and trade of a country, region, or society.

words.tr:
v. （使）连锁；（使）相互扣住
n. 互锁设备
words.ex: The puzzle pieces interlock tightly.
words.ex_cn: 拼图块紧密地互锁在一起。
words.en: To interlock means to fit together firmly or closely, or to cause things to fit together in this way.

words.tr:
v. 定罪；宣判有罪
n. 罪犯；囚犯
words.ex: The court convicted him of theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院判定他犯有盗窃罪。
words.en: If someone is convicted of a crime, they are found guilty of that crime in a court of law.

words.ex: The new policy is problematic for small businesses.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策对小企业来说成问题。
words.en: If something is problematic, it involves problems and is difficult to deal with or solve.

words.tr: adj. 可理解的；明白易懂的；清楚的
words.ex: His explanation was intelligible to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释人人都能听懂。
words.en: Capable of being understood; comprehensible.

words.ex: He sat by the window to ponder his future.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边深思自己的未来。
words.en: If you ponder something, you think about it carefully.

words.tr:
n. 真见鬼
int. 真见鬼
words.ex: What the heck is going on here?
words.ex_cn: 这到底怎么回事，真见鬼！
words.en: used to express surprise, frustration, or for emphasis

words.tr: n. 基本原理；基础理论；
words.ex: The rationale for the new rule is to save time.
words.ex_cn: 这个新规则的基本原理是节省时间。
words.en: The fundamental reasons or logical basis for a course of action or belief.

words.ex: The swamp is full of tall grass and frogs.
words.ex_cn: 这个沼泽里长满了高草和青蛙。
words.en: A swamp is an area of low-lying, uncultivated ground where water collects; a bog or marsh.

words.ex: The earthquake caused tremendous damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了巨大的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tremendous, you mean that they are very great in amount, extent, or intensity.

words.ex: The library keeps old newspapers in an archive.
words.ex_cn: 图书馆把旧报纸保存在档案馆里。
words.en: A collection of historical documents or records providing information about a place, institution, or group of people.

words.ex: He is overly careful with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱过于谨慎。
words.en: To an excessive degree.

words.tr: adj. 两种语言的；用两种语言的；
words.ex: He is a bilingual student who speaks English and Spanish.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个会说英语和西班牙语的双语学生。
words.en: A bilingual person is someone who can speak two languages equally well.

words.ex: The doctor can diagnose the illness quickly.
words.ex_cn: 医生能很快诊断出这种病。
words.en: If someone or something is diagnosed as having a particular illness or problem, their illness or problem is identified. If an illness or problem is diagnosed, it is identified.

words.tr: v. 使瘫痪；使麻痹；使无力
words.ex: The accident can paralyse a person.
words.ex_cn: 事故可能会使一个人瘫痪。
words.en: To paralyse means to make someone unable to move or act normally, often because of an injury or shock.

words.ex: He crammed the suitcase with clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服塞满了行李箱。
words.en: If you cram things or people into a place, you put them into it even though there is hardly enough room for them.

words.tr:
n. 常规；例行公事；
adj. 常规的；例行公事的；
words.ex: He follows a morning routine every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都遵循固定的惯例。
words.en: A routine is a sequence of actions regularly followed; a fixed program.

words.tr: adj. 繁重而累人的；艰苦的；使人精疲力尽的
words.ex: He ran a grueling marathon last Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他上周日跑了一场艰苦的马拉松。
words.en: A grueling activity is extremely difficult and tiring, often continuing for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 有竞争力的；竞争的；
words.ex: She is a competitive runner who wins many races.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有竞争力的跑步者，赢得了许多比赛。
words.en: Competitive is used to describe situations or activities in which people or firms compete with each other.

words.ex: He is a sophomore at Harvard University.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的二年级学生。
words.en: A sophomore is a student in the second year of college or high school.

words.ex: He could not conceive a world without technology.
words.ex_cn: 他无法设想一个没有科技的世界。
words.en: To conceive means to form or devise a plan or idea in the mind; to become pregnant.

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.ex: The shopkeeper will evaluate the old watch.
words.ex_cn: 店主将估价这块旧手表。
words.en: If you evaluate something or someone, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them, for example about how good or bad they are.

words.tr: phrase. 第三课第二组；第3课第2组
words.ex: The students in lesson 3 group 2 finished their homework early.
words.ex_cn: 第三课第二组的学生早早完成了作业。
words.en: A second designated set of students or participants in the third lesson of a course or training program.

words.ex: The ticket is your admission to the concert.
words.ex_cn: 这张票是进入音乐会的许可。
words.en: An admission is a statement in which you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, or the act of allowing someone to enter a place or organization.

words.tr: n. 差额；边缘；净利润；余地；
words.ex: The profit margin is five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 利润差额是五美元。
words.en: The margin is the edge or border of something, or the difference between two amounts, especially the difference between the cost of producing something and the price it is sold for.

words.tr:
n. 挑战；
v. 提出挑战；
words.ex: Climbing that mountain is a big challenge.
words.ex_cn: 爬那座山是一个巨大的挑战。
words.en: A challenge is something new and difficult which requires great effort and determination.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；决定性的；
words.ex: It is crucial to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水至关重要。
words.en: If you describe something as crucial, you mean it is extremely important.

words.ex: He frets about his exam results.
words.ex_cn: 他为考试成绩感到烦躁不安。
words.en: If you fret about something, you worry about it.

words.tr: adj. 中等的；次要的；第二的；
words.ex: He attends a secondary school in the city.
words.ex_cn: 他在城里上一所中学。
words.en: If you describe something as secondary, you mean that it is less important than something else.

words.tr: v. 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；
words.ex: Plants thrive in sunny places.
words.ex_cn: 植物在阳光充足的地方茁壮成长。
words.en: To thrive means to grow or develop well or vigorously.

words.ex: The movie was mediocre and not worth watching.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很平庸，不值得看。
words.en: If you describe something as mediocre, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.ex: He believes in an egalitarian society where everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他相信一个人人平等的平等主义社会。
words.en: Egalitarian is used to describe something that is based on the principle that all people are equal and deserve equal rights and opportunities.

words.ex: The school changed its curriculum last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年学校更改了课程。
words.en: A curriculum is the subjects that are studied in a school, college, or university.

words.ex: He showed great zeal in helping others.
words.ex_cn: 他在帮助他人时表现出极大的热情。
words.en: Zeal is great enthusiasm, especially in connection with work, religion, or politics.

words.ex: The affluent family bought a big house by the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这个富裕的家庭在湖边买了一栋大房子。
words.en: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.

words.ex: He compiles data from many surveys.
words.ex_cn: 他汇编来自许多调查的数据。
words.en: To compile means to collect information from different places and arrange it in a book, report, or list.

words.ex: The university has great prestige for its research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学因其研究而享有很高的声望。
words.en: The widespread respect and admiration felt for someone or something on the basis of a perception of their achievements or quality.

words.ex: We must eliminate the waste to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须消除浪费以保护环境。
words.en: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.

words.ex: The teacher gave students discretion to choose their own topic.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了学生自行选择题目的权利。
words.en: Discretion is the quality of behaving in a quiet and controlled way without drawing attention to yourself or giving away personal or private information.

words.tr: v. 绕行；设法避开；智胜；围住
words.ex: He circumvented the traffic by taking a small road.
words.ex_cn: 他通过走一条小路绕过了交通拥堵。
words.en: If someone circumvents a rule or restriction, they avoid having to obey it, usually in a clever and dishonest way.

words.ex: He is greedy and always wants more candy.
words.ex_cn: 他很贪婪，总是想要更多的糖果。
words.en: If you describe someone as greedy, you mean that they want to have more of something such as food or money than is necessary or fair.

words.tr:
n. 教养；养育；培育；
v. 培养；
words.ex: Her parents gave her good nurture.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母给了她良好的教养。
words.en: To nurture someone or something is to care for and encourage their growth or development.

words.tr:
n. 压力；强调；
v. 着重；强调；
words.ex: He feels stress from too much work.
words.ex_cn: 他因为工作太多而感到压力。
words.en: Stress is a state of mental or emotional strain or tension resulting from adverse or demanding circumstances.

words.ex: The old man muttered a curse under his breath.
words.ex_cn: 老人低声嘟囔了一句诅咒。
words.en: A curse is a word or sentence that is used to wish evil or harm on someone or something.

words.ex: The movie is a melodrama with crying and loud arguments.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部充满哭泣和激烈争吵的煽情剧。
words.en: A melodrama is a dramatic work in which the plot, typically sensational and designed to appeal strongly to the emotions, takes precedence over detailed characterization.

words.tr:
v. 发射；发起；启动；
n. 发射；投掷；启动；
words.ex: They will launch a rocket tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将发射一枚火箭。
words.en: To launch something means to send it into the air, space, or water, especially with a lot of force or effort, or to start an activity, event, or project.

words.tr:
adj. 乡村的；纯朴的；土气的
n. 乡下人；乡巴佬
words.ex: They live in a rustic cabin near the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一间乡村小屋里。
words.en: Rustic is used to describe things that are typical of the countryside rather than the town, or things that are simple and old-fashioned in a way that is considered typical of the countryside.

words.tr:
n. 组；群；集团；
v. （使）形成组；
words.ex: The students are in a group of five.
words.ex_cn: 这些学生组成一个五人小组。
words.en: A group is a number of people or things that are located, gathered, or classed together.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.ex: He eats gourmet food at a fancy restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家高档餐厅吃精致美食。
words.en: A gourmet is someone who knows a lot about food and cooking, and who enjoys eating high-quality food.

words.ex: We had a barbecue in the park last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们在公园举行了户外烧烤。
words.en: A barbecue is a meal or gathering at which meat, fish, or other food is cooked out of doors on a rack over an open fire or on a special appliance.

words.ex: The urban area has many tall buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市地区有许多高楼。
words.en: relating to a city or town

words.tr:
n. 兽群；
v. 放牧；
words.ex: The herd of cows walked slowly to the pasture.
words.ex_cn: 一群牛缓缓走向牧场。
words.en: A herd is a large group of animals of one kind that live together.

words.ex: The fugitive hid in the woods for weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这名逃亡者在树林里躲了几个星期。
words.en: A fugitive is someone who is running away or hiding, usually in order to avoid being caught by the police.

words.tr: n. 实际知识；技术；窍门
words.ex: He has the know-how to fix the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他有修理这台机器的诀窍。
words.en: Practical knowledge or expertise in a particular field or area.

words.tr: v. 迅速生长；急速增长
words.ex: The flowers burgeon in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天时，花朵绽放。
words.en: To grow or develop quickly; to flourish.

words.tr:
n. 群；蜂群
v. 云集；充满
words.ex: Bees swarm around the flower.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂围绕着花朵成群飞舞。
words.en: A swarm is a large group of insects, especially bees, moving together. As a verb, it means to move in or form a swarm.

words.ex: This restaurant is famous for its specialty, fried dumplings.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅以特色菜煎饺而闻名。
words.en: A specialty is a particular area of study or expertise that someone has, or a product that is particularly associated with a specific place.

words.ex: The company will deploy new software next week.
words.ex_cn: 公司将在下周部署新软件。
words.en: To deploy troops or military resources means to organize or position them so that they are ready to be used.

words.ex: He lives in a rural village with no big shops.
words.ex_cn: 他住在没有大商店的农村村庄里。
words.en: Rural areas are areas which are not towns or cities. They are often farming or agricultural areas.

words.tr: v. 反映；反射；反省；思考；仔细考虑；
words.ex: The mirror reflects the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 镜子反射阳光。
words.en: If a surface reflects light, heat, sound, or an image, it sends the light, etc. back and does not absorb it. If something is reflected in a mirror or in water, you can see its image in the mirror or in the water.

words.ex: He yearns for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他渴望更好的生活。
words.en: If you yearn for something, you want it very much.

words.ex: I reckon it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我认为明天会下雨。
words.en: If you reckon that something is true, you think that it is true.

words.ex: The water in the pond dwindles in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天时，池塘里的水逐渐减少。
words.en: If something dwindles, it becomes smaller, weaker, or less in number.

words.ex: The child loves to play with fantasy stories about dragons.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子喜欢玩关于龙的幻想故事。
words.en: A fantasy is a pleasant situation or event that you imagine, which is unlikely to happen.

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.ex: Sugar is an ingredient in this cake.
words.ex_cn: 糖是这个蛋糕的一个成分。
words.en: An ingredient is one of the substances that are combined to make something, especially in cooking.

words.ex: The artisan makes handmade pottery.
words.ex_cn: 这位工匠制作手工陶器。
words.en: An artisan is someone who makes things by hand, especially using traditional methods.

words.tr: v. 侵蚀；腐蚀；逐渐丧失；削弱
words.ex: The wind erodes the sand slowly.
words.ex_cn: 风慢慢侵蚀着沙子。
words.en: If rock or soil erodes or is eroded by the weather, sea, or wind, it cracks and breaks so that it is gradually destroyed.

words.tr: v. 向往；渴望；追求；立志
words.ex: He aspires to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他向往成为一名医生。
words.en: If you aspire to something, you have a strong desire to achieve it or attain it.

words.tr: phrase. 覆盖范围的文字说明；用于描述某项服务或产品覆盖区域的标注文字
words.ex: The map includes a coverage lettering that explains the service areas.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图包含了一段文字说明，解释了服务范围。
words.en: Text or lettering used to describe or provide information about an insurance policy's coverage.

words.tr:
v. 促进；使增长；
n. 提高；增强；
words.ex: Exercise can boost your energy.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进你的精力。
words.en: If one thing boosts another, it causes it to increase, improve, or be more successful.

words.tr:
n. 刻板印象；陈规老套
v. 对…存有成见；把…模式化
words.ex: He broke the stereotype that boys cannot cry.
words.ex_cn: 他打破了男孩不能哭的刻板印象。
words.en: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.

words.ex: The cat is agile and jumps high.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳得很高。
words.en: Someone who is agile can move quickly and easily.

words.tr:
v. 惊异于；惊异；
n. 令人惊异的人（或事）；
words.ex: I marvel at how fast she runs.
words.ex_cn: 我惊异于她跑得有多快。
words.en: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

words.ex: The elephant is gigantic compared to a dog.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象相比狗来说是巨大的。
words.en: If you describe something as gigantic, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size, amount, or degree.

words.tr: n. 并列争球；在扭夺的一堆人；拥挤的人群
words.ex: The rugby players formed a scrum to restart the game.
words.ex_cn: 橄榄球运动员排成并列争球以重新开始比赛。
words.en: In rugby, a scrum is a method of restarting play, involving players packing closely together with their heads down and attempting to gain possession of the ball. In software development, Scrum is a framework for managing and completing complex projects, particularly in software development, emphasizing teamwork, accountability, and iterative progress.

words.tr: v. 散发；发射（光或热）；辐射
words.ex: The sun radiates heat and light.
words.ex_cn: 太阳散发出热量和光。
words.en: To send out rays or waves, especially of light or heat; to spread out from a central point.

words.tr: n. 防御土墙；城墙；壁垒
words.ex: The old castle had a high rampart around it.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的城堡周围有一道高高的城墙。
words.en: A rampart is a wide, high wall of earth, stone, or other material built around a place to protect it from attack.

words.ex: The table is made of sturdy wood.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是用坚固的木头做的。
words.en: Someone or something that is sturdy looks strong and is unlikely to be easily injured or damaged.

words.ex: There was a scramble for the last ticket.
words.ex_cn: 大家争相抢购最后一张票。
words.en: If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you. Scramble can also mean to compete or struggle with others for something that is in short supply.

words.tr: n. 人性；人类；人道；仁慈；
words.ex: Kindness shows the best of humanity.
words.ex_cn: 善良展现了人性中最美好的一面。
words.en: Humanity refers to all human beings collectively or the qualities that make us human, such as kindness, compassion, and the ability to reason.

words.ex: They will extend the deadline by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他们将截止日期延长一周。
words.en: To extend something means to make it longer or larger, or to spread it over a larger area.

words.ex: He epitomizes the spirit of hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他体现了努力工作的精神。
words.en: To be a perfect example of a particular quality or type.

words.ex: He lives in a big metropolis with many tall buildings.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个有很多高楼的大都市里。
words.en: A metropolis is a very large city, often the most important city in a country or area.

words.tr:
adj. 动态的；有活力的；不断变化的；
n. 活力；动力；
words.ex: The game has dynamic weather that changes every hour.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏有每小时变化的动态天气。
words.en: If you describe someone as dynamic, you approve of them because they are full of energy or full of new ideas.

words.tr: v. 制定（法律）；通过（法律）；扮演（角色）
words.ex: The government will enact a new law next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将颁布一项新法律。
words.en: To enact a law or rule means to make it official by passing it through a legislative body.

words.tr: n. （宗教等的）仪式；例行习惯；
words.ex: The village holds a ritual every spring to pray for good weather.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄每年春天都举行一个仪式，祈求好天气。
words.en: A ritual is a religious service or other ceremony which involves a series of actions performed in a fixed order.

words.ex: The old song is reminiscent of my childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌让人想起我的童年。
words.en: If you say that one thing is reminiscent of another, you mean that it reminds you of it.

words.tr: adj. 沙哑的；粗声的；喧闹的
words.ex: His raucous voice made it hard to understand him.
words.ex_cn: 他沙哑的声音让他很难被听清楚。
words.en: A raucous sound is loud and harsh.

words.ex: The kids made a ruckus in the living room.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在客厅里闹出了很大的动静。
words.en: A ruckus is a noisy situation or argument.

words.ex: The letter revealed his secret.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他的秘密。
words.en: To reveal something means to make known something that was previously secret or unknown.

words.tr: v. 体现；使具体化；包含
words.ex: He embodies kindness and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他体现了善良和耐心。
words.en: To embody means to represent a quality or an idea exactly; to include or contain something.

words.ex: The boy defied his parents by staying out late.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因为熬夜不回家而违抗了父母。
words.en: If you defy someone or something, you refuse to obey them or you do something that they do not allow.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；例证；例示
words.ex: This example exemplifies the rule clearly.
words.ex_cn: 这个例子清楚地说明了这条规则。
words.en: To exemplify means to be a typical example of something or to give an example of something.

words.tr: phrase. 第4课第1组；第四课第一组
words.ex: He learns algebra in lesson 4 group 1.
words.ex_cn: 他在第四课第一组学习代数。
words.en: A designated set of students or participants in the fourth lesson of a course or training program.

words.ex: The significance of this discovery changed science.
words.ex_cn: 这一发现的重要性改变了科学。
words.en: The quality of being worthy of attention; importance.

words.ex: His opinion is subjective and not based on facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点是主观的，不是基于事实的。
words.en: Based on or influenced by personal feelings, tastes, or opinions.

words.tr: n. 头饰；头巾；头发编梳的式样
words.ex: She wore an elaborate headdress for the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 她为婚礼戴了一顶精致的饰头巾。
words.en: A headdress is a decorative covering or ornament worn on the head.

words.ex: The wedding ceremony was beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 婚礼仪式很美丽。
words.en: A ceremony is a formal event held on special occasions such as weddings, graduations, or official functions, often involving traditional or religious rituals.

words.ex: His perception of the sound was very sharp.
words.ex_cn: 他对声音的感知非常敏锐。
words.en: Your perception of something is the way that you think about it or the impression you have of it.

words.ex: The water supply is adequate for the village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对这个村庄来说是足够的。
words.en: If something is adequate, there is enough of it or it is good enough to be used or accepted.

words.ex: He is optimistic about the future.
words.ex_cn: 他对未来持乐观态度。
words.en: Someone who is optimistic is hopeful about the future or the success of something in particular.

words.tr:
n. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
v. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
words.ex: The car crash happened at the intersection.
words.ex_cn: 汽车碰撞发生在十字路口。
words.en: If a vehicle crashes or if the driver crashes it, it hits something and is damaged or destroyed.

words.tr:
n. 救援；营救；
v. 救援；营救；
words.ex: The rescue came just in time to save the hikers.
words.ex_cn: 救援及时赶到，救出了徒步者。
words.en: To rescue someone or something means to save them from a dangerous or unpleasant situation.

words.ex: The storm left only wreckage on the beach.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在海滩上只留下了残骸。
words.en: The remains of something that has been badly damaged or destroyed.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a big disaster.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了一场大灾难。
words.en: A disaster is an unexpected event causing great damage, destruction, or distress.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.ex: The Magna Carta is an old charter of rights.
words.ex_cn: 《大宪章》是一份古老的权力宪章。
words.en: A charter is a formal document describing the rights, aims, or principles of an organization or group of people.

words.tr: v. 批准；认可；通过；赞成(连of)
words.ex: My mom will approve my new phone.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈会同意我买新手机。
words.en: If you approve of an action, event, or suggestion, you like it or are pleased about it.

words.ex: Two countries signed a treaty to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 两个国家签署了一项条约以停止战争。
words.en: A treaty is a formal agreement between two or more countries or groups, especially one that is written down and signed by their leaders.

words.ex: He tries to mediate between the two friends.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在两个朋友之间调解。
words.en: To intervene between people or parties in order to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.tr: adj. 最终的；最后的；极端的；
words.ex: This is the ultimate solution to the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个问题的最终解决方案。
words.en: You use ultimate to describe the final result or aim of a long series of events.

words.tr: adj. 灭绝的；熄灭的；绝种的；
words.ex: The dodo is an extinct bird.
words.ex_cn: 渡渡鸟是一种灭绝的鸟。
words.en: If a species of animals or plants is extinct, it no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

words.ex: The medicine helped revive the sick man.
words.ex_cn: 这剂药帮助这位病人恢复了生机。
words.en: To revive something means to bring it back to life, consciousness, or use, or to make it active or successful again.

words.tr: adj. 复活的；复兴的；恢复活力的
words.ex: The resurgent economy is showing signs of growth.
words.ex_cn: 复苏的经济显示出增长的迹象。
words.en: If something is resurgent, it is becoming more popular or successful again after a period of being less popular or successful.

words.tr: v. 扫；“sweep”的现在分词； adj. 全面的；
words.ex: He sweeping the floor every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上扫地。
words.en: If you describe something as sweeping, you mean it is very extensive or has a very wide effect.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.ex: The assembly of the car took three days.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的装配花了三天时间。
words.en: An assembly is a group of people gathered together for a particular purpose, such as a meeting or a legislative session. It can also refer to the process of fitting together the component parts of a machine or other object.

words.tr: phrase. 第4课第2组；第4课第二组
words.ex: He learns algebra in lesson 4 group 2.
words.ex_cn: 他在第四课第二组学习代数。
words.en: A second designated set of students or participants in the fourth lesson of a course or training program.

words.ex: The power will devolve to the local government.
words.ex_cn: 权力将下放给地方政府。
words.en: If you devolve power, authority, or responsibility to a less powerful person or group, or if it devolves upon them, it is transferred to them.

words.tr:
v. 吹嘘；自吹自擂
adj. 一流的；极好的
words.ex: He brags about his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他炫耀自己的新车。
words.en: If you brag, you say in a very proud way that you have something or have done something.

words.ex: He showed great enthusiasm for learning English.
words.ex_cn: 他对学习英语表现出极大的热情。
words.en: Enthusiasm is a strong feeling of excitement and interest in something and a desire to become involved in it.

words.tr: adj. 压倒的；无法抗拒的；势不可挡的； v. “overwhelm”的现在分词；
words.ex: The crowd's cheers were overwhelming.
words.ex_cn: 人群的欢呼声压倒了一切。
words.en: If something is overwhelming, it affects you very strongly, and you do not know how to deal with it.

words.tr:
v. 刮；擦；刮出刺耳声；勉强通过
n. 刮；擦；擦痕；刮擦声
words.ex: He scraped his knee on the rough ground.
words.ex_cn: 他在粗糙的地面上擦伤了膝盖。
words.en: To remove something from a surface using a sharp or rough edge, or to injure a part of the body by rubbing it against a rough surface.

words.tr: n. 参与人（数）；装束；产量；清理
words.ex: The turnout for the election was very high.
words.ex_cn: 这次选举的投票率很高。
words.en: The number of people attending or participating in an event, especially a political meeting or election.

words.ex: The proportion of students who passed the test was high.
words.ex_cn: 通过考试的学生比例很高。
words.en: A proportion is a part of a whole, or the relationship of one part to another in terms of size, amount, or degree.

words.tr: n. 对应物；相当之物；副本；
words.ex: The CEO's counterpart in China signed the agreement.
words.ex_cn: 中国方面的对应人物签署了协议。
words.en: Someone's or something's counterpart is another person or thing that has a similar function or position in a different place.

words.tr: n. 装饰船头的人像；傀儡领袖；有名无实的首脑；
words.ex: The old ship had a wooden figurehead of a lion.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船的船头有一个木制的狮子像。
words.en: A figurehead is a person who is the head of an organization or country in name only, without any real power or authority.

words.tr:
n. 腐烂；衰落；
v. 腐烂；
words.ex: The fruit began to show signs of decay.
words.ex_cn: 这水果开始出现腐烂的迹象。
words.en: To decay means to be slowly destroyed by a natural process or to become gradually worse in quality, condition, or strength.

words.ex: He earned the esteem of his colleagues through hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作赢得了同事们的尊重。
words.en: If you esteem someone or something, you respect or admire them.

words.ex: He is an icon of pop music.
words.ex_cn: 他是流行音乐的偶像。
words.en: An icon is a small picture or symbol on a computer screen that represents a program or a file.

words.ex: The indigenous people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 本土居民住在森林里。
words.en: Indigenous people or things belong to the country in which they are found, rather than coming there or being brought there from another country.

words.ex: The birds live in a quiet marsh.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟生活在一片宁静的沼泽中。
words.en: A marsh is an area of low-lying land which is flooded in wet seasons or at high tide, and typically remains waterlogged at all times.

words.ex: Blue jeans are in vogue this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年牛仔裤很时髦。
words.en: If something is in vogue, it is very popular and fashionable.

words.ex: He met a compatriot at the airport.
words.ex_cn: 他在机场遇到了一位同胞。
words.en: A compatriot is a person from your own country.

words.ex: He plays rugby every Saturday.
words.ex_cn: 他每个星期六打橄榄球。
words.en: Rugby is a sport played by two teams of 15 players each, using an oval ball that players kick, pass, or carry in order to score points by grounding the ball behind the opponent's goal line or kicking it between the goalposts.

words.tr: n. 举办地点；（比赛）地点；会场；
words.ex: The concert will be held at a new venue.
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会将在一个新的举办地点举行。
words.en: A place where an event or meeting is held, such as a concert hall or conference center.

words.ex: The old tool fell into disuse after the new one was invented.
words.ex_cn: 新工具发明后，旧工具就被弃而不用了。
words.en: The state of not being used or practiced anymore.

words.tr:
n. 回声；
v. 回响；
words.ex: The echo came back from the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 回声从山上反弹回来。
words.en: An echo is a sound which is caused by a noise being reflected off a surface such as a wall.

words.ex: People vote in democracy to choose their leaders.
words.ex_cn: 人们在民主制度下投票选择他们的领导人。
words.en: A system of government by the whole population or all the eligible members of a state, typically through elected representatives.

words.ex: The movie was hilarious and made us laugh a lot.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影非常搞笑，让我们笑得很开心。
words.en: If you describe something as hilarious, you mean that it is extremely funny and it makes you laugh a lot.

words.tr: adj. 卷角的（书等）；（书页）折角的
words.ex: He has a dog-eared book on his desk.
words.ex_cn: 他的书桌上有一本翻旧了的书。
words.en: Having pages that are worn or turned down from use, especially a book.

words.tr:
v. 缓行；溜蹄
n. 溜蹄；缓行漫步
words.ex: He amble through the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后在公园里缓行。
words.en: To walk at a slow, relaxed pace, especially for pleasure.

words.tr: phrase. 第4课第3组；第4课的第3小组
words.ex: The students in lesson 4 group 3 are doing their homework.
words.ex_cn: 第4课第3组的学生们正在做作业。
words.en: A third designated set of students or participants in the fourth lesson of a course or training program.

words.ex: He scan the QR code with his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他用手机扫描了二维码。
words.en: To look at something carefully or quickly in order to find out specific information or to examine something thoroughly.

words.ex: He carries a brown satchel to school.
words.ex_cn: 他背着一个棕色的书包去学校。
words.en: A satchel is a bag with a long strap, traditionally used for carrying books.

words.tr: adj. 奇怪的；奇数的；余的；
words.ex: He wore an odd hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇怪的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odd, you mean that they are strange or unusual.

words.ex: The soldier threw a grenade into the enemy bunker.
words.ex_cn: 士兵把一颗手榴弹扔进了敌人的掩体。
words.en: A grenade is a small bomb that can be thrown by hand or launched from a rifle.

words.ex: He wore a big grin after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得比赛后露出了灿烂的咧嘴笑容。
words.en: If you grin, you smile broadly, usually showing your teeth.

words.tr:
v. 大口喝；狂饮
n. 痛饮；一大口
words.ex: He swigged the soda quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速地喝了一大口苏打水。
words.en: To take a swig means to drink something quickly in large mouthfuls.

words.ex: He wields his knowledge to solve problems.
words.ex_cn: 他运用自己的知识来解决问题。
words.en: To wield something means to hold and use it, especially as a weapon or tool. It can also mean to have and be able to use power or influence.

words.tr: v. 戒绝；弃权；自我克制
words.ex: He abstains from eating sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他戒食糖。
words.en: If you abstain from something, you deliberately do not do it or have it, especially something you like or enjoy which might be considered bad for you.

words.ex: He has a small mustache.
words.ex_cn: 他有一小撮胡子。
words.en: A mustache is a strip of hair left to grow above the upper lip.

words.tr: adj. 狂怒的；暴怒的；激烈的
words.ex: He was furious when he lost his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了钥匙时非常生气。
words.en: If someone is furious, they are extremely angry.

words.tr: adj. 统治的；支配的； v. “rule”的现在分词；
words.ex: The ruling class controls the government.
words.ex_cn: 统治阶级控制着政府。
words.en: A ruling is an official decision made by a judge or court, or a decision made by someone in authority.

words.tr: n. 埃米尔（伊斯兰教领袖的尊称）
words.ex: The emir rules his desert kingdom wisely.
words.ex_cn: 埃米尔英明地统治着他的沙漠王国。
words.en: An emir is a title of high-ranking Muslim rulers or military leaders, especially in the Middle East.

words.ex: He opposes the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他反对这项新法律。
words.en: If you oppose someone or something, you disagree with them and try to prevent them from doing something, or you try to change what they are doing.

words.ex: The wound began to swell after the insect bite.
words.ex_cn: 被昆虫叮咬后，伤口开始肿胀。
words.en: To increase in size or volume as a result of internal pressure; to expand.

words.ex: He is a conservative man who likes old traditions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢古老传统的保守男子。
words.en: A conservative person or group is one that does not like changes or new ideas, especially in politics or religion.

words.ex: He is an ambassador to France.
words.ex_cn: 他是驻法国的大使。
words.en: An ambassador is an official envoy, especially a high-ranking diplomat who represents a state and is usually accredited to another sovereign state or to an international organization as the resident representative of their own government or sovereign or appointed for a special and often temporary diplomatic assignment.

words.ex: He obsesses over small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他 obsesses 于微小的错误。
words.en: If something or someone obsesses you, you think or worry about them all the time and you cannot think about anything else.

words.tr:
n. 等价物；
adj. 相等的；等价的；
words.ex: The dollar is the equivalent of ten yuan.
words.ex_cn: 美元是十元的等价物。
words.en: If one amount or value is the equivalent of another, they are the same.

words.ex: The Philippines is an archipelago of thousands of islands.
words.ex_cn: 菲律宾是一个由数千个岛屿组成的群岛。
words.en: An archipelago is a group of islands, especially small islands, scattered in a body of water.

words.ex: He volunteers for civic projects in his town.
words.ex_cn: 他为家乡的市民项目做志愿者。
words.en: Relating to a city or town, especially its administration; relating to the duties or activities of people in relation to their town, city, or local area.

words.tr:
v. 调情；轻率地对待
n. 与多人调情的人
words.ex: He flirts with her at the coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他在咖啡店向她调情。
words.en: If you flirt with someone, you behave as if you are sexually attracted to them, in a playful or not very serious way.

words.ex: It is a taboo to speak his name in this village.
words.ex_cn: 在这个村子里，提到他的名字是禁忌。
words.en: A taboo is a social or religious custom prohibiting or restricting a particular practice or forbidding association with a particular person, place, or thing.

words.tr:
adj. 红外线的
n. 红外线
words.ex: The remote uses infrared to change the TV channel.
words.ex_cn: 遥控器使用红外线来切换电视频道。
words.en: Infrared refers to the region of the electromagnetic spectrum with wavelengths longer than visible light but shorter than microwaves, often used in technology for night vision and heat sensing.

words.ex: He puffed after running up the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 他跑上楼梯后喘着气。
words.en: If you puff, you breathe in and out quickly and with force, for example because you have been running or because you are out of breath. A puff of something such as air or smoke is a small amount of it that is blown out from somewhere.

words.tr: phrase. 第四课第四组；第四课中的第四小组
words.ex: He learns algebra in lesson 4 group 4.
words.ex_cn: 他在第四课第四组学习代数。
words.en: A designated section or set of activities within a learning sequence, specifically the fourth group in the fourth lesson.

words.tr:
v. 发牢骚；抱怨；轰鸣
n. 怨言；牢骚；轰隆声
words.ex: He grumbles when he has to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不早起时就会抱怨。
words.en: If someone grumbles, they complain about something in a bad-tempered way.

words.tr: n. 投票；选举权；参政权
words.ex: Women won suffrage in 1920.
words.ex_cn: 女性在1920年获得了选举权。
words.en: Suffrage is the right to vote in political elections.

words.ex: He fastened the strap around his wrist.
words.ex_cn: 他把带子系在手腕上。
words.en: A strap is a narrow piece of leather, cloth, or other material that is used to fasten, secure, or carry something, or to hold onto something.

words.ex: A sliver of wood stuck in his finger.
words.ex_cn: 一小片木头扎进了他的手指。
words.en: A sliver is a small, thin piece of something that has been cut, broken, or torn off from a larger piece.

words.ex: Honesty is a great virtue.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种伟大的美德。
words.en: A virtue is a good quality or way of behaving.

words.ex: Farmers spread mold on the fields to enrich the soil.
words.ex_cn: 农民把粪肥撒在田里以肥沃土壤。
words.en: A soft, fine-grained soil; also a hollow or cavity, or a container for shaping something.

words.ex: The castle is a medieval building.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是一座中世纪的建筑。
words.en: Relating to the Middle Ages, the period in European history from about the 5th century to the 15th century.

words.tr: n. 骑士精神；骑士制度；
words.ex: He showed chivalry by helping the lady carry her bags.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助那位女士提包，展现了骑士精神。
words.en: Chivalry is a set of qualities such as bravery, courtesy, honor, and gallantry toward women, associated with the medieval institution of knighthood.

words.ex: He studied heraldry to understand his family's coat of arms.
words.ex_cn: 他学习纹章学以理解他家族的盾徽。
words.en: The study or art of creating, granting, and blazoning arms and related insignia, especially as practiced in medieval times.

words.tr:
n. 名声；名誉；名望
v. 认为；以为
words.ex: He is of good repute in his town.
words.ex_cn: 他在镇上声誉很好。
words.en: The opinion generally held of someone or something; the state of being regarded in a particular way.

words.tr:
v. 称赞；恭维
n. 称赞；恭维
words.ex: He gave her a compliment on her dress.
words.ex_cn: 他夸了她的裙子。
words.en: A compliment is a polite expression of praise or admiration.

words.ex: The queen's reign lasted 70 years.
words.ex_cn: 女王的统治持续了70年。
words.en: The period during which a sovereign rules; to hold royal office; to prevail

words.tr: n. 高超的技艺；造诣；英勇；
words.ex: His prowess in basketball amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在篮球方面的高超技艺让所有人都惊叹。
words.en: Exceptional skill or ability in a particular field or activity.

words.ex: The police discovered a scheme to steal money.
words.ex_cn: 警方发现了一个偷钱的阴谋。
words.en: A scheme is a plan or arrangement, especially one produced by a government or other organization, or a secret plan to do something, especially something illegal or dishonest.

words.tr: adj. 精致的；微妙的；易碎的；脆弱的；
words.ex: She wore a delicate lace dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精致的蕾丝连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is delicate is small and beautifully shaped. It can also be easily broken or damaged.

words.tr:
n. 肌腱；力量的来源
v. 给…以力量
words.ex: The sinew held the muscle to the bone.
words.ex_cn: 肌腱将肌肉连接到骨头。
words.en: A sinew is a tendon, the strong tissue that connects muscles to bones, or it can refer to the strength and energy that makes someone able to do something difficult.

words.ex: The surgeon's dexterity saved the patient's life.
words.ex_cn: 外科医生的灵巧救了病人的命。
words.en: Skill and grace in physical movement, especially in the use of the hands; adroitness.
